title: [Technical] Audit and harden the Supabase migration baseline
body:
## Objective
Validate and harden the single squashed pre-production Supabase baseline before any remote integration.

## Scope
- Apply `202610120001_baseline.sql` from zero in disposable local Supabase.
- Review table purpose, constraints, UTC boundaries, invoker security, grants, revocations, and default privileges.
- Verify RLS on every exposed table and run the pgTAP access tests.
- Add tests for zero votes, ties, duplicate votes, disabled questions, finalization, and missing records.
- Confirm no shared or production database consumed the discarded prototype migrations.

## Acceptance criteria
- Local reset, database tests, and database lint succeed from an empty database.
- Automated tests prove active results cannot leak and finalized votes cannot mutate.
- Remote dry-run contains only the baseline migration and the fresh-project strategy is approved.

## Depends on
T01.

title: [Technical] Add Supabase read-only health connectivity
body:
## Objective
Prove safe mobile-to-Supabase connectivity before reading or writing product data.

## Scope

- Configure `EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` and the publishable key only.
- Add typed configuration validation and a harmless health endpoint/query.
- Render missing-config, connecting, success, and failure states.

## Security constraints
Never embed a secret/service-role key, database password, FCM credential, or translation API key.

## Acceptance criteria
- Android and iOS development builds connect successfully.
- Missing or invalid configuration fails clearly.
- Bundle inspection finds no server secrets.

title: [Technical] Implement an idempotent secure vote write path
body:
## Objective
Accept one immutable server-confirmed vote per installation and question.

## Scope
- Use a secured Edge Function or RPC to validate question status, UTC window, and YES/NO input.
- Issue and verify an installation credential; do not trust arbitrary client device IDs or fingerprints.
- Enforce uniqueness, rate limits, and idempotency/replay handling server-side.
- Derive network abuse signals server-side and return an immutable vote receipt ID.

## Acceptance criteria
- Duplicate, late, malformed, and replayed requests are rejected deterministically.
- A retry returns the original accepted receipt rather than adding a vote.
- The UI records only server-confirmed votes.

T04 and T02.

- Offline voting cannot appear accepted.

title: [Technical] One-time consent-based device history import at verified account creation
body:
Replace automatic every-session history claims with a server-enforced first-verified-signup entitlement, bound to the originating device/session and frozen eligible history. Use the owner-selected checked-by-default checkbox; make no pre-OTP account-enumerating email lookup. Existing accounts on any later device restore canonical account history only. Applied requests retry idempotently; declined consent stays declined. Import only server-accepted unowned votes, never arbitrary local records or another account's answers. No changes to existing vote totals/choices.

Resolved former gap: automatic every-session history claims are retired and imports require the server-issued signup entitlement. Separate device security associations from history ownership so new guest votes after logout are not attributed to the last signed-in account. Test same/different-device signup races, shared devices, response loss, decline then re-login, account deletion/recovery and privacy-safe used-device receipts. See points 4–5 and 26.

title: [Feature] Brewing submission/upvote journeys, daily rules and discoverable views
body:
Guests browse/share; verified members submit one question and upvote one other person's question per UTC day. Keep self-upvote and global daily allowance checks on the server. Repeated support for the same still-open question on different days is allowed; totals are accumulated events, not unique supporters. Upvotes use full-question confirmation/cancel, one in-flight request, server receipt/reconciliation and a selected marker; other upvotes remain unavailable with an exact UTC reset reason/date. A conditional login wait is a separate reason, not an already-used vote.

Top-right + opens a dedicated Ask screen; Back preserves context/draft. Unavailable + remains accessible/tappable for explanation (a native disabled button cannot show a tap tooltip). Proposed new-source limit 180 graphemes, matched client/server counting, neutral yes/no tips and daily-slot information; preserve old/translated wording. T21 covers public typeahead and pending AI triage. List/grid defaults list and field-wise saved preferences. All open candidates persist across days; community ranking alone chooses midnight winner, later submissions win equal totals. Moderator removal stays audited and cannot nominate the next question. See points 13,15–16,21.

title: [Research] Define minimum sample and reliability rule for any future country result
body:
## Decision needed
What minimum evidence is required before showing a country-level split?

## Constraints
Country reporting is deferred and must not be inferred from phone code, locale, SIM, or IP. A future implementation requires optional self-declared country, privacy review, anti-switching controls, and honest “PULSE voters in X” labels.

## Research scope
- Choose a minimum sample threshold and whether it varies with margin of error.
- Define copy: `Not enough votes for a reliable country result.`
- Suppress percentages and winner below threshold.
- Evaluate small-cohort privacy and manipulation risk.
- Require sample size and unweighted-sample disclosure above threshold.

## Acceptance criteria
A written product/statistical/privacy decision is approved before country data or UI is implemented.

## Out of scope
Implementing country collection now.

title: [Research] Threat-model device eligibility and duplicate voting across devices
body:
## Decision needed
Define enforceable device eligibility, session behavior, and duplicate-vote policy without implying that a device equals a human.

## Stress-test scenarios
- The same email signs in on two physical devices before either session refreshes.
- One person uses several physical devices, reinstalls, clears storage, restores backups, or clones app data.
- One person uses a different verified email on every device.
- Devices are shared, lost, offline, or transferred while a vote is in flight.
- Account history and installation history contain conflicting votes for one question.

## Critical constraints
The product rule is one accepted vote per eligible physical device and question. Supabase single-session enforcement does not establish device identity. Installation secrets do not survive every reinstall. Platform attestation can reject many scripts/emulators but is not a permanent cross-platform device ID. Device fingerprints are mutable, spoofable, and privacy-invasive.

## Research scope
- Model abuse economics, false positives, accessibility/shared-device harm, offline races, recovery, reinstall, and transfer.
- Evaluate App Attest, DeviceCheck, Play Integrity, device recall, request binding, rate limits, risk scoring, verified accounts, and sampling.
- Specify transactional conflict policy and auditable idempotency.
- Decide whether strict reinstall prevention requires verified accounts where platform recall cannot supply a stable guarantee.

## Acceptance criteria
An approved threat model, exact public product claim, data-flow/privacy review, platform support matrix, conflict matrix, and abuse-response plan exist before enforcement.

## Out of scope
Treating CAPTCHA, email, a local secret, or a client-generated identifier as proof of a physical device.

title: [Research] Design secure anonymous Pulse transfer with a QR handoff
body:
## User outcome
A non-account user can intentionally transfer eligible local/server-known Pulse history to a new device.

## Security requirements
- Never encode a raw device ID, installation secret, email, auth token, or history payload in the QR code.
- Prefer a server-issued, one-time, short-lived, audience-bound transfer challenge.
- Require confirmation on the old device, authenticated claim on the new installation, replay protection, expiry, cancellation, and credential rotation.
- Define whether the old installation is revoked, retained read-only, or can recover after an interrupted transfer.
- Define conflict handling, lost/broken old device behavior, screenshots of QR codes, clock skew, offline states, and support/audit controls.

## Acceptance criteria
A reviewed protocol and abuse/privacy model demonstrates atomic transfer, no replay, no secret disclosure, and deterministic recovery.

## Out of scope
Implementation before T06/T07 installation credentials and receipts exist.

title: [Legal/Product] Complete global youth safety, age-rating, and launch-country review
body:
## Decision needed
Define where and for whom PULSE can legally and safely launch.

## Ruthless premise check
App Store/Play age ratings and parental controls are distribution aids, not a transfer of the developer's legal duties. `No adult content` does not eliminate child-privacy, consent, profiling, notification, UGC/moderation, retention, deletion, advertising, dark-pattern, or local-content risks. Adult questions may also change ratings and country availability.

## Scope
- Obtain qualified counsel and build a country-by-country launch matrix for age thresholds, parental consent, data rights, and restricted topics.
- Decide age assurance/minimum-age UX without collecting unnecessary sensitive data.
- Define question/submission moderation, escalation, reporting, crisis topics, election/health claims, and emergency takedown.
- Complete store questionnaires/ratings, privacy disclosures, retention/deletion/export policy, notification consent, analytics/ads decision, and incident response.
- Test youth-comprehensible copy, accessibility, coercion/dark-pattern risk, and parental-control behavior.

## Acceptance criteria
Legal/product/security sign-off exists for each launch country, unsupported regions are blocked appropriately, and policies/operations are live before youth marketing.

## Out of scope
Assuming stores alone enforce every country's law.

title: [Security] Complete global launch abuse and operations gate
body:
## Objective
Take the gateway-only vote path from a secure baseline to a globally operated service.

## Scope
- Validate App Attest and Play Integrity server-side with privacy review; voting must fail closed when required verdicts are unavailable or invalid.
- Add gateway/IP/ASN risk controls without storing raw network identifiers longer than necessary.
- Add dashboards, alerts, kill-switch drills, secret rotation, load/penetration tests, runbooks, and rollback exercises.
- Publish an honest unweighted PULSE-participant methodology; state the one-eligible-physical-device rule and its measured reinstall limitations precisely.

## Acceptance criteria
Independent security review, capacity test, incident drill, privacy sign-off, and launch SLOs pass.

## Note
The repository now has a gateway, database kill switch, hashed installation credentials, and bounded per-installation attempts. Attestation and production operations require external platform/infrastructure configuration and remain open.

title: [Technical] Canonical account history and account/device separation through logout
body:

An existing account restores its own canonical history, never automatically imports a new device's guest answers. History links and device anti-abuse relationships are separate. New guest votes after logout must remain unowned instead of being credited to the last bound installation account. Clearing private caches does not erase authoritative quotas; do not expose an earlier account's choices through guest receipt recovery.

Cover many accounts on a shared device, one account on many devices over time, import decline, lost-response replay, deletion/recovery, immutable totals and minimum private association retention. Keep already accepted votes authoritative and avoid a generic two-way overwrite. See points 4–5,10,26.

title: [Security] Independent account/device duplicate guards and protected physical-device actions
body:
Keep device/question and account/question uniqueness, session generation, idempotency and request-bound server verification. Guest daily votes use the device guard; signed-in votes use both. A login-day delay is not a substitute and cannot deduplicate repeated requests from an already eligible session. Retain honest one-device/account limits without claiming one unique human. No universal stable device ID or perfect reinstall resistance is promised.

Extend protected gateway/attestation/risk handling to Brewing upvotes and deprecate the unprotected direct authenticated write path. New guest votes must not inherit the last account's ownership. Recommend tablet support; store filters/sideload restrictions are not integrity proof, and attestation is not a universal phone-vs-tablet classifier. Private account/device-session mapping is many-to-many, minimal and retention-bounded. For upvotes, propose an additional device/day cap (shared-device exclusion requires owner approval). See points 2,7,10,13–15,26 and the offline counterexamples.

title: [Security] Risk-based CAPTCHA assurance without physical-device or lifetime-session claims
body:
CAPTCHA is bot friction, not proof of physical hardware, identity or a unique human. Provider tokens are short-lived/single-use and cannot authorize unlimited later actions. Design a separate server-issued scoped/expiring assurance signal if reducing repeated puzzles, plus fresh request-bound integrity checks according to platform protocol.

Step up on new/suspicious sessions/devices, replay/velocity/risk or assurance expiry; do not remove current per-vote CAPTCHA until an equivalent reviewed control ships. Gate the write after verification, cover provider outage/accessibility/false positives, and do not challenge public browsing/sharing. Link T17 and T10. See points 13–14.

title: [Research] Evaluate device + verified email + verified phone voting
body:
## Product direction
Move PULSE closer to **one person, one vote** after anonymous device voting has proven adoption and after a measured, reviewed rollout. Perfect proof of personhood is not promised. The goal is to make duplicate voting materially harder by requiring all three independent controls: a server-recognized eligible device, a verified email address, and a verified phone number.

## Proposed identity and voting invariants
- A login succeeds only after separate, short-lived OTPs sent to both the normalized email address and normalized E.164 phone number are verified in the same server transaction.
- One verified phone can bind to only one verified email, and one verified email can bind to only one verified phone. The resulting immutable internal `person_identity_id`—not either raw value—is the voting identity.
- A persistent session may vote daily without repeating both OTPs. New sign-in, account recovery, sensitive identity changes, or risk escalation requires both factors again.
- Vote acceptance requires a currently valid identity session **and** the eligible-device controls from T17.
- The database enforces one accepted vote per question for both `person_identity_id` and recognized device. Application checks are not sufficient.
- Email/phone changes require re-verification, a cooling-off period, notification to both old channels where possible, session revocation, abuse review, and auditable recovery.

## Required scenarios
1. **Normal login:** the user enters both OTPs. The email/phone pair becomes exclusive. Once the session is established, the user can vote daily without recurring OTP friction until logout, expiry, revocation, recovery, or risk escalation.
2. **Same device, different identity pair:** after the device votes, logout followed by a different verified email/phone pair cannot create another vote for that question because device uniqueness has already been consumed.
3. **Same identity pair, different device:** after the identity votes, login on another eligible device cannot create another vote for that question because identity uniqueness has already been consumed. The second device may participate on later questions subject to policy.
4. **Concurrent race:** simultaneous requests from multiple devices for the same identity, or multiple identities from the same device, result in exactly one accepted vote through database uniqueness and transactional locking.
5. **Reinstall/reset:** device recall/fingerprint/attestation controls reconnect the device where supported; identity uniqueness still blocks a second vote after login when device recall is unavailable.
6. **Dual-SIM/multiple-email attacker:** different legitimate pairs and different physical devices may bypass the model. Measure this residual risk; do not claim it is eliminated.
7. **Shared/recycled phone:** family/shared numbers, reassigned numbers, lost access, SIM swap, number porting, and deceased/inactive owners require explicit recovery and dispute rules without silently transferring voting history.
8. **Aliases and normalization:** email aliases/case rules, Gmail-style plus addressing, internationalized domains, E.164 normalization, VoIP/temporary numbers, carrier changes, and country-code ambiguity must have deterministic policy. Do not implement provider-specific alias collapsing casually.
9. **Account lifecycle:** test logout, session theft, refresh-token replay, lost device, remote session revocation, email-only loss, phone-only loss, deletion, export, legal hold, and re-registration after deletion.
10. **Availability and inclusion:** test SMS/email delay or outage, travel/roaming, sanctioned or unsupported regions, users without SMS service, accessibility, minors, and support escalation. No silent fallback may weaken both-factor verification.

## Ruthless premise check
The combination will substantially raise the cost of casual duplicate voting, but it still does not prove one natural person. A motivated actor can obtain several devices, SIMs, and emails; SIM farms and synthetic identities exist. Conversely, one-phone-per-email can exclude families, schools, refugees, travelers, low-income users, and users of recycled numbers. The assumption that bypassers are a small percentage must be tested with evidence rather than embedded as a security premise. Download count or traffic alone is not an adequate rollout trigger.

## Research and rollout scope
- Define measurable abuse, integrity, participation, exclusion, support-cost, and geographic-bias thresholds that justify collecting phone numbers.
- Compare this proposal with passkeys, platform attestation/device recall, carrier intelligence, account reputation, privacy-preserving proof-of-personhood, and transparent device-based sampling.
- Complete threat modelling, DPIA/privacy review, telecom/vendor review, country launch matrix, retention/deletion policy, breach response, and qualified legal review.
- Prototype in an isolated environment, then run opt-in and observe-only experiments before staged enforcement. Keep an immediate rollback path.
- Decide whether raw email/phone values remain solely with authentication vendors; application tables should prefer opaque identity IDs and minimum derived metadata.
- Publish methodology as **one verified identity-and-device vote**, not one-human-one-vote, unless a separately reviewed proof-of-personhood system justifies that stronger claim.

## Acceptance criteria
- Database and concurrency tests prove one accepted vote per question across both recognized device and `person_identity_id`.
- Both OTPs are required for every new authentication ceremony and sensitive identity change; sessions are securely persisted, revocable, and risk-step-up capable.
- All scenarios above have approved outcomes, recovery rules, user copy, telemetry, privacy controls, and abuse/support runbooks.
- A measured pilot shows material fraud reduction with acceptable participation loss, accessibility, geographic bias, false rejection, cost, and support burden.
- Security, privacy, legal, product, and operations owners approve staged rollout and public claims.

## Do not implement yet
Keep the current anonymous/device phase until R01, R03, T14, T16, T17, and T19 are operationally proven and this research gate passes. Do not collect phone numbers merely because PULSE crosses an arbitrary download or traffic threshold.

title: [Operations] Deploy monitoring, alerts, and recurring incident drills
body:
## Objective
Turn the repository monitoring primitives and runbook into continuously verified production operations.

## Implemented foundation
- Privacy-safe structured vote gateway events with request IDs and bounded reason/status fields.
- Authenticated `operational-health` Edge Function backed by a service-only aggregate health RPC.
- Optional critical alert webhook delivery and a repository readiness guard.
- Incident response runbook covering kill switch, secret compromise, CAPTCHA outage, alert delivery, finalizer replay, and rollback.

## Remaining external work
- Configure a Supabase log drain, dashboards, retention/access controls, primary and backup alert destinations, and an external uptime caller in every environment.
- Set SLOs and tested thresholds for absence of health checks, latency/errors, rejection anomalies, question cardinality, scheduler/finalization lag, and alert-delivery failure.
- Execute quarterly drills and retain evidence; remediate every failed objective by an owned deadline.
- Add independent load and penetration tests and verify the monitoring pipeline during those tests.

## Acceptance criteria
Production and staging generate actionable alerts to two destinations, a synthetic check detects whole-project failure, on-call ownership is documented, and every required drill has recent evidence with detection/recovery times. No sensitive identifier or token enters logs or alerts.

## Depends on
T14, T15, production Supabase deployment, and an approved monitoring provider.

title: [Technical] Benchmark vote storage/read models before partitioning at projected scale
body:
Keep one logical indexed votes table and finalized question_results snapshots rather than one independently managed table per question. Benchmark real read/write mixes, midnight contention, history, index/row sizes, retention/WAL/backups and pool limits before declarative time/hash partitioning. Preserve global account/device/idempotency uniqueness and question-date FKs across partitions.

Model 1K/100K/1M/100M daily active voters with explicit participation/burst/storage assumptions; no price or single-instance capacity guarantee. Table statistics are not exact authoritative vote totals. Limit public polling/counter hot rows and use bounded cached read models. Source arithmetic: docs/requirements/capacity-and-storage.md; model is not a hosted load test. See point 25.

title: [Feature] Multilingual question suggestions and pre-publication review workflow
body:
Start with debounced/cancelable indexed lexical/full-text/trigram/prefix retrieval over public Brewing/live/Past Results. Test language-specific normalization/tokenization and negation/paraphrases; semantic AI is a later measured option, not a per-keystroke default. Suggestions route to the exact highlighted screen and retain draft/back context. Exact active duplicates need transactional protection; near matches suggest rather than auto-block, and historical questions can repeat as new dated occurrences.

Before public upvotes/sharing, apply format/abuse checks and asynchronous AI triage with durable Pending, provider timeout/retry, uncertain-human-review, same-slot edit/appeal and strict API-cost/rate controls. One UTC-day submission slot is reserved at accepted intake, not by typing or cancel. Midnight eligibility uses published_at, never retroactively includes post-boundary publication. Measure multilingual false-positive/negative quality before rollout; no real-time moderation SLA is assumed. See point 21.
